Backtest parameter sweeps — 2023-07-24 to 2026-07-22

2160 configs = concentration_cap × risk_aversion (λ) × optimizer_lookback (240 combinations) replayed across all 9 max_watchlist_size curation sets. These knobs touch only the mean-variance replay, not the curator, so the whole grid costs $0 (no LLM — the curations already exist; only expanding max_watchlist_size itself, section 6, re-curates). Metrics are benchmark-relative: Information Ratio = annualized active return ÷ tracking error vs SPY (consistency of beating the benchmark). SPY returned +71% over the window. ★ = best in column.

All in-sample. These rank candidate configs to forward-test; they don't prove an optimum. Read the IR t-stat (|t|>2 ≈ real vs luck), the bootstrap CI (error bar on annualized return), and H1/H2 stable (does the edge hold in both halves) before trusting any row.

Parameter settings

The three swept knobs (every combination = 240 configs) and the values considered. All other optimizer / backtest params are held at the investor_profile.md values — these knobs only re-weight the same curations.

parametervalues sweptcurrent (profile)
concentration_cap0.5, 0.67, 0.8, 0.9, 1.01.0
risk_aversion (λ)0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 4.02.0
optimizer_lookback (days)14, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150150
max_watchlist_size (re-curation, §6)2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 126

1. Return vs drawdown

The horizontal axis is max drawdown — the portfolio's biggest peak-to-trough loss as a fraction of its running peak (the single worst high-to-low decline over the window); further right = deeper loss. The vertical axis is annualized return, so upper-left is best (high return, shallow drawdown). Each point is one cap/λ/lookback config; color = max_watchlist_size (2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 12 shown), so every watchlist size contributes its own 240-config cloud (total 2160 points). Within a cloud the free knobs move a point deterministically; jumping between colors ALSO swaps the underlying curation, and those kimi re-curations swing 2-5× on their own — so read cross-color separation as parameter effect + curation-draw noise, not a clean mws response. The canonical live config (watchlist 6) is the black star.

2. Return vs L1 churn

Same points (all watchlist sizes), risk axis replaced by L1 churn = annualized one-way turnover (%/yr): how much of the portfolio is traded per year (Σ|Δweight| from share changes; drift between rebalances is not a trade). 100%/yr = the whole book turned over once a year. This is the industry-standard churn measure. Trading is free in an IRA, so read it as stability/robustness, not cost: lower churn = less noise-chasing / less overfit, so upper-left (high return, low churn) is the sweet spot. Current config: 706%/yr.

3. Return vs L2 course correction

Same idea, but churn is the L2 (Euclidean) path length the portfolio was dragged along through weight-space (√Σ Δweight² per rebalance, summed & annualized) — your “total course-correction”. Vs L1, it weights concentrated single-name rotations more heavily. It ranks these configs almost identically to L1 (correlation 0.98), which is the useful takeaway: the two norms agree, so the churn ordering is robust. Current config: 907/yr.

4. Recommended settings

Read straight off plots 1-3: keep only configs in the safe corner — |maxDD| < 45% AND L1 < 800 AND L2 < 1000 (shallow drawdown, low churn on both norms). 372 of 2160 configs survive (by watchlist size — 2:82, 3:112, 4:45, 5:32, 6:42, 7:25, 8:16, 10:7, 12:11), listed once, sorted by IR. ★ = best in that column among the survivors, so you can eyeball the top IR / t-stat / Sharpe / Calmar / ann / shallowest-DD without re-sorting. These stay in-sample — a forward-test shortlist, not an auto-switch. Note the live config (ws 6 1.00/2.0/150d, dd 38% / L1 706 / L2 907) passes and is listed below (highlighted).

5. Portfolio value over time — by max_watchlist_size (vs buy/hold and SPY)

Each re-curated watchlist cap's realized portfolio value on the same pools and starter — the equity-curve view of the section-9 sweep. Tighter (smaller) watchlists concentrate into the top picks; wider ones dilute across more next-wave names.

6. max_watchlist_size sweep

Unlike the cap/λ/lookback knobs above (free math replays on one curation set), max_watchlist_size changes the curator's decisions, so each cap is a separate re-curation (~$0.40 LLM each) on the same news pools and AAPL/GOOGL/AMZN starter. The bar is each curation's total return; the QUBT / RKLB / NVDA columns flag whether that curation ever added those tickers (yes = entered the watchlist; proposed-rejected = tried but blocked).

adds/removes = the curator's proposals that the validator APPLIED; rejects = proposals still blocked after retries (double-add, add to a full watchlist with no paired remove, or a stale remove); retries = reject-and-retry rounds fired (the validator told the curator why a proposal was rejected and it re-proposed). Rejects should be ~0; retries shows how much correction that took. A large reject count means decisions are being silently blocked (the symptom that exposed the max_watchlist_size cap-override bug).

7. news_lookback_days sweep

Another CURATOR-param sweep (re-curation), but title-only — the curator reads the preserved GKG article titles only, with NO Wayback or live-fetch, so each window is a zero-network re-curation on the same corpus at the canonical mws 6 / cap 1.0 / λ 2.0 / 150d config. The bar is each window's total return; the QUBT/RKLB/NVDA columns flag whether that window's curation added those tickers. Wider windows surface more-established (higher-coverage) stories; narrower ones favor fresh breakouts.

8. Backtest gems

For every ticker the curator ever held, its best $ gain (price-driven P&L on the position) across all 1350 sweep settings, and the setting that produced it. A ticker's gain is maximized by the config that weighted it most while it ran (usually high cap, low λ, short lookback). Note the $ figure is compounding-weighted: a late-window winner rides an already-grown balance at up to 100% concentration, so it dwarfs early picks — these are hindsight, in-sample upper bounds, a gem list to build a low-churn strategy around, not a track record. 12. LLM comparison — curator model (same pools + profile config)

Every model reads the same news pools and replays at the profile config (cap 0.8 / λ 2.0 / 30d); the only variable is the curator LLM. The decision columns are the ones that matter: agree = share of weeks the model made the identical add/remove call as the default model (top row, kimi), valid-JSON = share of calls that parsed, $/run = curator LLM cost of a full 157-week curate, and curator time = wall-clock of those 157 calls (≈ per-call latency × 157; excludes GKG ingest + optimizer replay). Backtest columns are secondary (in-sample / leaky). A cheap model that tracks the default makes the whole non-zero-cost sweep affordable.

14. Rationale-soundness — blind judge (leak-free)

Every backtest column above (return, IR, Sharpe, Calmar, t-stat) is in-sample — the curator could have memorized which 2023–2026 names later won, so those numbers can't honestly rank reasoning. This section does: an independent judge (claude-opus-4-8, not one of the curators) reads each add/remove blind — model identity stripped, decisions shuffled, and the ticker's later price never shown — and grades only whether the stated rationale + cited news justified the call at the time. Five criteria (each pass/fail) + a holistic overall 1–5. 72 decisions judged, ~$0.58. Ranked by mean overall — this is the one ranking here that owes nothing to hindsight.

curatoroverall (1-5)naddremoveon-thesisevidencecatalystdisciplinevalid-ticker
kimi-k2.54.2584.753.7588%88%75%100%100%
claude-sonnet-54.00164.123.88100%81%69%88%100%
deepseek-v4-flash3.77484.083.4696%71%71%73%94%

overall = mean 1–5 soundness · add/remove = mean overall split by action · the five % columns = share of that curator's decisions passing each criterion: on-thesis (maps to a named wave), evidence (cited news actually supports the claim), catalyst (concrete milestone, not noise), discipline (buildup-not-crest; a remove is justified, not churn), valid-ticker (real investable US listing, not a name/delisted/false-match).
